newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA CABINET IMPOSES 15 PCT GRAIN EXPORT TAX.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA CABINET IMPOSES 15 PCT GRAIN EXPORT TAX.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday decided to impose a 15 percent grain export tax until the end of the year to offset further grain shortages, a government Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said.
"A grain export tax comprising 15 percent of the international grain price will be imposed," Kostov told reporters.
The cabinet set a minimum grain purchase price from producers at 230,000 levs or $134 per tonne, he added.
The World Bank agreed with Bulgaria's proposal to introduce a temporary tax on grain exports, which will phase out by year-end.

Bulgaria freed prices and trade rules in line with agreements with the Bank and the International Monetary Fund reached two months ago. But pending grain shortages have prompted the government to seek partial protectionist measures.

Preliminary estimates show Bulgaria needs to import more than a million tonnes of grain to cover the gap until next year's crop after uncontrolled grain exports two years ago caused a grave grain crisis earlier this year. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
